## Corrected finding and evidence

**Documentation/support gap: an observed macOS Node 26 native-driver build failed at the SDK linker; a consistent local CLT compiler/linker/SDK selection now builds successfully. Linux Node 26 works in the supplied parity run.** This issue no longer treats the dependency's declared engine range as evidence of general Node 26 incompatibility.

The owner's Linux aarch64 report, completed 2026-10-23, states:

> Both main-branch full npm test runs passed.
>
> All 8 isolated installs and all 8 full builds passed.
>
> No installation, build or subprocess-launch failure occurred in this matrix.

Main was exactly `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`. Both `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run build`, and full `npm test` passed on **Node 24.13.0 and Node 26.12.1**, with independently installed native bindings in isolated worktrees. The 26.12.1 patch substitution is explicit. These are owner-supplied devbox results, not a Linux rerun by this gap-hunt supervisor.

The earlier macOS arm64 run used **Node 26.12.0 / npm 11.20.0**, with a fresh dependency on `better-sqlite3@12.9.0`:

- No matching prebuilt binary was found, so installation attempted a source build.
- node-gyp downloaded Node headers and SHASUMS successfully with HTTP 200.
- The source build reached the installed macOS SDK linker and failed with `tapi error: malformed file` / `unknown architecture` in `libSystem.tbd` and `libc++.tbd`.

That is the observed macOS-specific host/toolchain failure. It is **not a missing-header failure**, does not establish that every macOS Node 26 installation fails, and is contradicted as a universal Node 26 failure by the successful Linux run. The subsequent bounded toolchain control below resolves this local build failure without changing the driver or engine range.

## macOS toolchain control and shared-store result (2026-10-23)

[Complete evidence and exact command-local recipe](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/6d3f3f3/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/node26-clt/REPORT.md), preserved on `gap-hunt-durability@6d3f3f3`, now narrows the diagnosis further:

- The original linker could not parse the newer CLT SDK stub architecture `arm64e.x1`; the captured failure says `tapi error: malformed file` and `error: unknown architecture` in `libSystem.B.tbd` / `libc++.1.tbd`. Node headers had downloaded successfully (HTTP 200).
- Selecting only `DEVELOPER_DIR` and CLT PATH initially produced a separate `stdio.h not found` failure. One bounded retry selected absolute CLT `CC`/`CXX`, `SDKROOT` and `-isysroot` compile/link flags consistently. With unchanged locked `better-sqlite3@12.9.0`, Node26.12.0 `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, package build and native SQLite open/query/close all passed. No global `xcode-select` change or tool installation occurred.
- Independently installed Node24.22.1 and Node26.12.0 checkouts at identical source `bbd2c1ef779ea8ef05ca80bf17c6b2be04aa8209` have distinct native binary paths/checksums. Both **24→26→24 and 26→24→26** sequences on one store per sequence passed: body calls **1→0→0**, published→reused→reused, identical exact result locator and nested Unicode payload. The supervisor independently repeated this runner successfully.

The raw runner concludes:

> PASS: both independently installed cross-version shared-store sequences preserve bodies, payload and exact references

These are bounded macOS arm64 results. They establish neither universal macOS compatibility nor Linux same-store cross-version reuse. The driver still emits `EBADENGINE` because its metadata excludes Node26; successful execution does not amend that upstream declaration. Keep this warning, prebuild availability, local source-build prerequisites, and actual runtime evidence distinct.

## Governing consumer need and scope

A consumer needs platform-qualified native installation guidance: tested Node/platform combinations, native prebuild/source-build prerequisites, and a useful diagnostic when an SDK cannot link the driver. Public memory-store compatibility remains separate from private-alpha durable-backend evidence.

The published driver declares `20.x || 22.x || 23.x || 24.x || 25.x`, while the facade/Machine Node manifests say `>=20`. This remains a **metadata discrepancy**, not proof of runtime incompatibility or a reason to narrow engine ranges in this task. The adapter uses better-sqlite3 unconditionally; built-in `node:sqlite` is not a fallback.

## Reproduction and controls

Evidence branch and one-command native diagnostic: `gap-hunt-durability@faa7d25`. With the selected Node26 version and npm on PATH, run from a clean evidence checkout:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/diagnose-158-native.mjs
```

It creates a disposable pinned native consumer, records platform/version/install output, and opens SQLite if installation succeeds. The unchanged runner has now been executed from a clean detached evidence checkout on macOS arm64 Node26.12.0/ABI147 using the consistent command-local CLT compiler/linker/SDK environment. Actual child install and native smoke both exit0, with `native-sqlite-open-query-ok`; clean-before/after and complete output are [preserved here](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/faa7d25/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/node26-clt/DIAGNOSTIC-158.md). The outer diagnostic exit alone is not the success oracle. The historical macOS failure and supplied Linux full-suite results remain separate observed outcomes. It does not require or fabricate a failure. A working compiler/toolchain and registry access are prerequisites when no prebuild exists.

The original macOS failure and positive Node24 cold/restart controls remain in [the captured portability evidence](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/447d798c7bd65b1d09e597dbdec1eb5f6944bb06/scratch/gap-hunt/portability). The metadata-only `verify-158.mjs` at `gap-hunt-durability@10affd562b2642f714f671d0a03435d873693b5d` diagnoses manifest declarations only and must not be described as a failing native/runtime test.

Linux evidence: [owner-provided Linux parity report preserved unchanged](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/e475049/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/owner-linux-parity.md), with [provenance and coverage limits](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/e475049/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/LINUX-PROVENANCE.md).

The Linux report uses independent installations/stores. It proves native installation and full-suite execution on the tested Linux versions, not reusing one persisted store interchangeably across Node versions. Newer hunt fixtures absent from the report's pinned branches also remain outside its coverage.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. Document the observed macOS Node26.12.0 SDK linker failure with actual diagnostics and successful header downloads, plus the verified command-local compiler/linker/SDK recipe that resolved it. Preserve the intervening header-discovery failure as separate evidence. Avoid blanket Node26/macOS or missing-Node-header diagnoses; do not change global toolchain selection.
2. Quote and link the Linux aarch64 success at `c5802da` on Node24.13.0/26.12.1: independent native installs, builds and full `npm test` pass. Keep tested behavior distinct from declared dependency metadata and universal platform support.
3. Give a disposable native install/open diagnostic that records Node, OS, architecture, installation result and relevant linker/binding output. Successful native installation must remain a valid outcome; do not hard-code an expected Node26 failure.
4. Preserve public memory-store behavior and supported native controls; explain native prebuild/source-build requirements, separate #157's pnpm build-approval workflow, and do not imply built-in SQLite supplies a fallback.
5. Do not change engine ranges, swap/upgrade drivers, add an adapter, alter release automation, or publish packages under this documentation task. Any such runtime support decision requires a separate contract and conformance evidence.

Pickup-ready for bounded documentation/diagnostic work. Blocking dependencies: none; coordinate adjacent wording with #157. Out of scope: universal macOS failure claims, generic Node26 incompatibility, universal cross-version shared-store certification, upstream SDK repair, and runtime-policy changes.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex gap-hunt workers (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North, authored the original synthetic installation evidence and replay artifacts.
Agent assistance: Supervising Codex reviewed the original linker logs and the owner-provided Linux parity report, corrected the interpretation, independently repeated the bounded macOS shared-store runner, and updated this issue. The Linux runs are attributed to the supplied devbox report; no claim is made that this supervisor reran them or that a human reviewed implementation.

comments.body: Documentation pickup contract added with five numbered criteria, negatives and scope boundaries. From `gap-hunt-durability@10affd562b2642f714f671d0a03435d873693b5d`, run `node scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/verify-158.mjs`. Metadata checks confirm the declared support mismatch; this does not establish native installation or cross-version execution. No blocking issue dependency; coordinate adjacent wording with the paired native-install issue. Do not change engine ranges, drivers, alpha support or published releases under this task. Agent assistance: gpt-6.1-sol worker prepared the evidence; supervising Codex reviewed the bounded handoff.

**Correction from owner-supplied Linux parity evidence (2026-10-23): this is an observed macOS SDK linker failure, not general Node26 incompatibility.**

At main `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`, Linux aarch64 **Node24.13.0 and Node26.12.1 both pass native dependency installation, full build and full `npm test`** with independently installed bindings. The report states: “Both main-branch full npm test runs passed.” It also states: “All 8 isolated installs and all 8 full builds passed” and “No installation, build or subprocess-launch failure occurred in this matrix.”

The earlier macOS arm64 Node26.12.0 installation downloaded headers successfully (HTTP200), then failed in the installed SDK linker with `tapi error: malformed file` / `unknown architecture` in `libSystem.tbd` and `libc++.tbd`. That is the platform/toolchain-specific observed failure; it is neither missing headers nor proof that all Node26 or all macOS hosts fail. The declared driver range remains metadata and must not be used to infer runtime incompatibility. Same-store cross-version reuse was not exercised by the independent Linux installations.

The pickup contract is being narrowed to platform-qualified native prerequisites/diagnostics and these explicit positive controls. No engine narrowing or driver change is authorized. Agent assistance: supervising Codex reviewed and quoted the owner-provided parity report; this is not a claim that this supervisor reran Linux.

Pickup update: the Linux evidence remains full `npm test` PASS on aarch64 Node24.13.0 and26.12.1. The macOS26.12.0 linker failure is now bounded to the captured local SDK/toolchain setup: a command-local consistent CLT compiler/linker/SDK recipe builds the same locked driver successfully. Independent same-source installations pass shared-store24→26→24 and26→24→26 with body calls1→0→0 and exact-reference/payload equality; I independently repeated that runner. [Logs and exact recipe](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/6d3f3f3/scratch/gap-hunt/contract-operations/node26-clt/REPORT.md).

For pickup, document the observed failure and verified setup while preserving the upstream Node26 engine warning as metadata. No engine narrowing, driver changes, or global toolchain changes are authorized. Linux shared-store parity and pnpm approval remain separate. Agent-authored evidence and review; no human review claimed.

title: Document native SQLite toolchain setup and macOS Node 26 linker diagnostics
